title: Elementwise criterion for a cocone of a filtered diagram of modules to be a colimit
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, $\mathcal I$ a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and $i\mapsto M_i$ a functor from $\mathcal I$ to the category of $R$-modules, with transition maps $M(a):M_i\to M_j$ for $a:i\to j$. Let $N$ be an $R$-module and $q_i:M_i\to N$ $R$-linear maps with $q_j\circ M(a)=q_i$ for every morphism $a:i\to j$ of $\mathcal I$ (a cocone). Assume: (1) every element of $N$ is $q_i(x)$ for some object $i$ and some $x\in M_i$; (2) for every object $i$ and all $x,y\in M_i$ with $q_i(x)=q_i(y)$ there is a morphism $f:i\to k$ of $\mathcal I$ with $M(f)(x)=M(f)(y)$ (equivalently, since the maps are linear: $q_i(z)=0$ implies $M(f)(z)=0$ for some $f:i\to k$). Then $(N,(q_i)_i)$ is a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto M_i$ in the category of $R$-modules.

source.place: Categories, Section 04AX (label section-directed-colimits, lines 2124-2176): for a filtered diagram the colimit is the disjoint union modulo 'eventually equal'; for modules Algebra, Lemmas 00D6 (label lemma-directed-colimit, algebra.tex line 778) and 00D7 (label lemma-zero-directed-limit, algebra.tex line 811). The criterion is the converse direction: the canonical map from the colimit to N is surjective by (1) and injective by (2).
